Technology stocks were starting to trim some of their prior declines, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 losing over 0.2% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was continue to sink almost 1.7%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(-) Jabil Circuit ( JBL ) retreated Tuesday, at one point falling over 10%, despite reporting core fiscal Q4 net income and revenue exceeding Wall Street expectations. Excluding one-time items, the company earned $0.70 per share, improving on a $0.64 per share core profit during the year-ago period and beating the Capital IQ consensus by $0.02 per share. Revenue rose to $5.77 billion from $5.02 billion last year and also topping the $5.41 billion analyst mean.
In other sector news:
(+) XO Group ( XOXO ) rose as much as 26% on Tuesday after the digital marketplace company agreed to a $933 million merger and going-private transaction led by private equity investors Permira Funds and Spectrum Equity. Under terms of the proposed buyout, XO Group investors will receive $35 in cash for each of their shares, representing a 27% premium to Monday's closing price. The operator of The Knot ecommerce web site also will be merged with WeddingWire, which like The Knot, targets wedding customers. The transaction is expected to close during the first half of 2019.
(-) CenturyLink ( CTL ) slipped nearly 9% on Tuesday after saying chief financial officer Sunit Patel will step down on Sept. 28 to accept an executive position at another company. The networking services company has named Neel Dev, currently its group vice president for finance, to assume Patel's former duties on an interim basis and will soon begin an internal and external search for a permanent finance chief.
